acceptance: A deliberately hung test or session-finish hook in a throwaway CI run produces, in the job log, the stacks of every worker and the process tree, and the job fails within 5 minutes of the hang starting, naming the stuck node id or phase.
Normal medium-test runs are unaffected: wall time is within 2% of the previous week's median for the same shard.
If the dump on a real recurrence identifies a cause (leaked process, thread, or fixture teardown), a regression test covers it.
Decision gate: if the hang does not recur within two weeks of the diagnostics landing, finish with the diagnostics only and record a deferral naming the evidence to collect next time.
description:
Problem. On PR #4039, CI run 42431461560 (merge commit 4952dd265e68480436132dfb6f4f156e5d50bea5), medium-test (shard 2) was cancelled at the job timeout three times: attempts 1-3, each about 25 minutes. In attempt 2 the shard reached 99% at 02:17 and then sat idle until 02:34. The resource monitor showed the xdist workers alive, with steady RSS and the load average falling toward 0.1. The per-test --timeout=60 never fired, so the hang is outside a test call: likely session or xdist teardown, a leaked child process, or a non-daemon thread. The same shard passed on the previous merge commit (run 42427026571), and passed again after the PR was closed and reopened for a fresh merge ref. The cancelled suite then blocked arming ('hidden behind a newer success'), which needed a rerun-then-cancel to clear. Nothing in the log names what was stuck, and the run burned about 75 runner-minutes.

Change.
(1) Before the job timeout, dump every pytest and xdist worker's Python stacks, plus the process tree, into the job log, for example with a watchdog step using py-spy dump or faulthandler via a signal.
(2) End the run with a non-zero exit that names the stuck phase or test.
(3) Fix the root cause if the dump identifies it.

Guardrails: work in a linked worktree (make worktree-create); never edit the primary clone; stage paths explicitly; no explanatory comments or docstrings (make comment-policy-check); heavy work only via make heavy-run, never forcing admission; never bypass a required check, ruleset, hold label or review gate; re-read cited files on current origin/develop first. The repo refuses pytest's faulthandler_timeout locally (tests/conftest.py); do not re-enable it there. Do not raise the job timeout.
